habitat: Bushveld and woodland with sparse grass or stony ground, especially mopane, and also Acacia savanna and the edges of wooded drainage lines.
summary: A common resident of Kruger woodland. Eastern birds, including those in the lowveld, are the browner, slender-billed form. Adults are well streaked above and on the breast, with a white eyebrow, no rufous wing edges, and white to pale-buff outer tail feathers. The sexes are not described as differing. Newman’s family note says immature larks are generally more speckled; a species-specific juvenile or chick colour is not given.

similar.note: Fawn-coloured Lark has rufous upperparts and whiter underparts. Sabota Lark is more heavily streaked on the breast and has no rufous wing edges.
Monotonous Lark has a rufous wing panel and an eyebrow that stops short of the bill. Sabota Lark’s white eyebrow is present in every race.

bill.shape: slender in the eastern race; thicker in the arid west

head.pattern: white eyebrow, distinctive in every race

upperparts.pattern: well streaked above; brownest in the east

wings.pattern: no rufous edges on the wing

tail.shape: outer feathers white to pale buff

viewNotes.note: Streaked brown upperparts without a rufous wing panel. The outer tail feathers are white to pale buff.
The underwing is not described. The song may also be given in hovering flight.
A white eyebrow and a streaked breast. Eastern birds have a slender bill.
Well-streaked brown upperparts and pale outer tail feathers. The rump is not given a separate colour.
The white eyebrow, streaked breast and plain wing, without rufous edges, show in profile. It often sings from a tree.

calls.description: A high, melodious and variable song of notes, whistles, trills and buzzy sounds, including imitations of other birds, from a tree or in hovering flight; the texts used here do not assign it to one sex.

research.note: Status is resident. SABAP1 found no seasonal movement, with only local shifts after rain, so all twelve months are listed. Kruger birds belong to the eastern, slender-billed group. Eye, leg and belly colours are not named. Chick colour is not described. The grade A song was recorded in the Kruger area. The account names rastor and copper are the iNaturalist account names.
